The process involves three participants: a Customer, a Manufacturer, and Suppliers.

The process begins on the Customer side when the customer selects the properties of a chainsaw they wish to order. This selection is sent to the Manufacturer, who receives and analyzes the order.

Upon analyzing the order, the Manufacturer orders the necessary parts, sending this request to the Suppliers. The Manufacturer then awaits receipt of the parts from the Suppliers. Once parts arrive, a check is made to determine if all parts have been received. If not all parts have arrived, the Manufacturer checks with the Suppliers and then continues to receive parts until the order is complete.

Once all parts are received, a manual inspection is conducted. Following the inspection, the chainsaw is assembled. During assembly, regular updates are sent to the Customer. After assembly, the first product is sent to the Customer for evaluation.

The Manufacturer then awaits feedback from the Customer. Based on the feedback received, one of two paths is followed: either the product needs improvement, in which case improvements are made and the revised product is sent again to the Customer for another round of feedback, or the product is satisfactory.

When the feedback is positive, two activities happen simultaneously: the rest of the order is produced while progress is monitored. During production, regular updates continue to be sent to the Customer. Once both the production of the remaining order and progress monitoring are complete, the complete order is sent to the Customer.

On the Customer side, the order is received, and the process concludes for the Customer. The Manufacturer's process also ends after sending the complete order.

This process describes a job recruitment workflow involving three participants: a Company, a Job Seeker, and a Job Platform.

**Company's Process:**
The process begins when the company receives a job application. Upon receiving it, two activities happen simultaneously: the company confirms the job application and rates the job application. Once both activities are completed, a decision is made. If the application is declined, the process ends with no employee found. If accepted, the company negotiates an interview with the job seeker. Following the interview, the company rates the job seeker and decides whether to proceed. If declined, the process ends with no employee found. If accepted, the company hires the prospective candidate, and the process concludes successfully with an employee found.

**Job Seeker's Process:**
The job seeker's process starts by reporting their application status. They then go through available job offers and submit an application. After applying, the job seeker awaits a response. If declined, they return to reporting their application status and continue searching. If accepted, they enter a probation phase. After the probation, the job seeker rates the company. If the company is rated C or less, the job seeker returns to browsing job offers. If the company is rated above C, the job seeker transitions to a permanent job, concluding their search successfully.

**Job Platform's Process:**
The platform's process begins by sending job offers to job seekers. It then analyzes reports received from job seekers about their application status. The platform forwards applications to companies. Following this, two activities occur in parallel: receiving the application rating and receiving the job confirmation from the company. Once both are received, if declined, the platform returns to sending job offers. If accepted, the platform proceeds to receive the seeker rating from the company and the company rating from the job seeker in parallel. After receiving both ratings, if the company rating is above C and the seeker was accepted, the process ends with a successfully conveyed job. The process begins when a student has a desire to register for a USI course.

The student selects a course, and the application checks if slots are free for that course. If no slots are available, the student must select a different course. If slots are free, the application shows the available dates.

The student then selects one date and checks if an account at the sports institute is available. If an account is already available, the student proceeds directly to log into the account. If no account is available, the student checks if they are registered at an eligible university.

If the student is registered at an eligible university, they register with a new account and then proceed to log in. If the student is not registered at an eligible university, they send a request for activation and wait for a response. After receiving the response, they proceed to log into the account.

Once logged in, the student provides payment information. The application then completes the registration for the course. Following this, two activities happen simultaneously: the student tweets their friends about the registration, and the application sends a ticket to the student.

Once both the tweeting and ticket receipt are complete, the process ends.

The process begins when a customer has a wish to build a house.

The customer first collects requirements for the house project. After collecting the requirements, the customer sends these requirements to the Architect. The customer then waits until a draft is received from the Architect.

Once the draft arrives, the customer checks its feasibility. A decision is then made whether the draft is sufficient. If the draft is not sufficient, the customer refines the requirements and sends them again to the Architect, repeating this cycle until a satisfactory draft is obtained.

When the draft is deemed sufficient, a check is made whether the project is subject to approval. If approval is required, the customer reports for a building permit. After obtaining the permit, or if no approval was needed, the customer creates an order list and places the order with Amadon.

After placing the order, the effort is calculated. Then two parallel paths begin: the customer waits to get the order from Amadon, and simultaneously a decision is made whether the project is affordable.

If the project is not affordable, the customer calls friends for assistance. If the project is affordable, the customer hires a building company. Both paths then converge.

Once the order is received from Amadon and either friends have been called or a building company has been hired, the house is built. The process concludes when the house is finished.

Once the order is received, it is processed, and then two activities occur simultaneously: building the airplane base model and transmitting the customization requirements to the responsible teams (the Team).

After both the base model is built and the requirements have been transmitted, a 14-day waiting period begins. Following this waiting period, a check is performed to determine if the requirements have been met.

If the requirements are not met, a reminder is sent to the responsible team, and the process returns to the 14-day waiting period before checking the requirements again.

If the requirements are met, the individual bits and pieces are installed in the airplane according to the customization specifications. Once installation is complete, the engines and risk factors are controlled, and then the plane is prepared for a test flight.

A test flight protocol is received from the Test Pilot, and this information is automatically forwarded to the Customer.

Next, a determination is made regarding the type of shipping. If the customer is a premium customer, the airplane is shipped via premium shipping. Otherwise, standard shipping is used for delivery to the customer.

After either shipping method is completed, the Manufacturer receives a confirmation via email from the Customer, and the process ends.

Following this, two activities happen simultaneously: the airplane base model is built, and the requirements for the customization are transmitted to the responsible Team. After both of these activities are completed, a 14-day waiting period begins.

After the waiting period, a check is made to determine if the requirements have been met. If the requirements have not been met, a reminder is sent to the responsible Team, and then the 14-day waiting period restarts. If the requirements have been met, the individual bits and pieces are installed in the airplane.

Once the installation is complete, the engines and risk factors are controlled. The plane is then prepared for a test flight. After preparation, a test flight protocol is received from the Test Pilot.

The protocol is then automatically forwarded to the Customer. At this point, the process splits based on the customer type. If the customer is a premium customer, the airplane is shipped via premium shipping. Otherwise, standard shipping is used.

After either shipping method is completed, a confirmation is received via E-Mail from the Customer, and the process concludes.

The process begins when a user opens Battle.net.

At this point, a check is made to determine if the user is already registered. If the user is not registered, they enter their account information and then click on the link in the confirmation email received from Battle.net. After confirming their registration, the process continues to the login step.

If the user is already registered, they proceed directly to log into Battle.net. Once logged in, the account information is loaded automatically.

Next, the system checks whether the World of Warcraft subscription is active. If the subscription is not active, the user selects a payment method. Depending on the chosen payment method, the user either enters credit card information or enters their IBAN and BIC for bank account payment. After completing the payment details, the process continues to the game login.

If the subscription is already active, the user proceeds directly to log into the game. Once logged in, the in-game data and position are loaded automatically.

Following this, three activities happen simultaneously: the user selects a realm, selects a race, and selects a class. Once all three selections are complete, the user names their character.

After naming the character, Battle.net sends confirmation and selfies to the user, which are received by the system. The process then concludes.

The Machine process begins at the start, where the machine is run. After running, the connection is checked. If the machine is disconnected, the process ends. If the machine is connected, information and measurements are collected, followed by calculating the OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness).

Based on the OEE calculation, the process takes different paths. If the OEE is good, the process loops back to collecting information and measuring again, continuing the monitoring cycle.

If the OEE is too low, two activities occur simultaneously: the machine is stopped, and an e-mail is sent to the engineer. Once both the machine has been stopped and the e-mail has been sent, this branch of the Machine process ends.

Meanwhile, the Engineer process begins separately. The engineer starts by checking mails. Upon receiving the e-mail from the machine about low OEE, the engineer finds the inefficient equipment, then fixes the equipment. After the repair, the engineer manually starts the machine, which triggers the machine to run again. The Engineer process then ends.

The communication between the two participants occurs when the machine sends an e-mail to notify the engineer about efficiency issues, and when the engineer starts the machine after completing repairs.

The process describes an inspection workflow involving two participants: an Inspector and an Application system.

The Inspector begins by entering the type of machine and serial number. This information is sent to the Application, which receives the type and serial number. Upon receiving this data, the Application queries the relevant questions based on the machine information, then asks these questions back to the Inspector.

The Inspector answers the questions and then hits next. This action triggers the Application to autofill values relevant to the specific machine. The Application then shows these values to the Inspector.

The Inspector checks the values displayed and then confirms the values, sending this confirmation to the Application. The Application receives this confirmation and evaluates whether the inspection is complete.

If the values are confirmed as correct (Yes), the Application marks the inspection as done, and the Application's process ends. Meanwhile, the Inspector finishes the inspection, concluding their part of the process.

If the values are not confirmed (No), the Application loops back to query relevant questions again, and the cycle of asking questions, showing autofilled values, and checking continues until the Inspector confirms the values are correct.

This process describes a car service inspection system involving three participants: a Police App, a Mechanic, and a Car Owner.

The process in the Police App begins after a successful service, following which there is a waiting period. Then the system checks if the car is still registered. If the car is not registered, the process ends. If the car is registered, the car owner is notified, which triggers a notification to the Car Owner.

The Car Owner receives the app notification and can either bring their car to service or ignore the notification. If the owner ignores the notification, they will receive a fine from the Police App, and their part of the process ends there.

If the Car Owner decides to bring the car to service, this initiates the process at the Mechanic and also starts parallel activities for the owner: waiting for the car to be repaired and receiving status updates.

When the car arrives at the Mechanic, the mechanic checks the car and enters any car problems found. The problems are communicated to the Police App, which then offers payment to the car owner. Simultaneously, the mechanic sends updates to the Car Owner and begins repairing the car. Once both the updates are sent and the repair is complete, the mechanic determines the payment amount and communicates this to the Police App.

Meanwhile, the Police App decides how to handle the payment. If payment is via the app, the payment is transferred to the mechanic, followed by receiving confirmation of successful repair. For other payment methods, the system proceeds directly to receive confirmation of successful repair. After receiving confirmation, the system receives the time for the next service and the process terminates.

Back at the Car Owner's side, once both the waiting period and status updates are complete, the owner chooses to pay either via the app or with cash/card. If paying cash or by card, this payment is sent to the Mechanic. After payment, the Mechanic receives the payment, enters that the repair succeeded, and provides the customer with the Pickerl (inspection sticker). The Mechanic then enters the time for the next service, which is communicated to the Police App, completing the Mechanic's process. The Car Owner receives the Pickerl from the Mechanic, and their process ends.

If the Police App detects no car arrival at the mechanic after checking, there is another waiting period, after which the car owner is fined, and that branch of the process ends.

If not already reported, a task is added to contact the Labour Inspectorate. These parallel paths then merge before proceeding.

If no one was killed or severely injured, a task is added to contact superiors, and the process continues.

The system then checks if the victim has private insurance. If yes, a task is added to contact private insurance. Regardless of this outcome, the system proposes all accumulated tasks to the user.

The user then executes the proposed tasks, and the process ends when everything is done.

When the waiting period ends, the bot checks if a random natural event has happened. If yes, the bot is reset and then continues farming. If no random natural event occurred, the bot starts farming directly. Both farming paths lead to checking whether a new milestone has been achieved.

If a new milestone is achieved, the player is notified automatically, and the player then reads the message. After reading the message, or if no milestone was achieved, the process checks whether the bot has finished.

If the bot is not finished, it is given a sleeping break, and the cycle continues with waiting for random natural events again.

If the bot is finished, one or more actions may occur: the player may brag to friends about the achievement, or help others with materials, or both. Once these optional activities are completed along with the resource list update, the process concludes and ends.
